nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, let $c \in \alpha$, and write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ and contains $\varphi(c)$, then $\Delta$…
nodes.title: Universal formulas from Henkin witnesses

nodes.summary: If $C$ is a nonempty family of sets of formulas that is totally ordered by inclusion and every member of $C$ is consistent, then the union $\bigcup C$ is consistent.
nodes.title: Unions of chains of consistent sets are consistent

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $L_F$ be the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$, with inclusion $\iota : L_F \to L$. If $F$ is consistent, then so is the preimage of $F$ in $L_F$: the set of formulas $\psi_0$ of $L_F$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ whose image $\iota(\psi_0)$ under the inclusion belongs to $F$.
nodes.title: Consistency passes to the finite-symbol sublanguage

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $\alpha$ a type of variables. A set $S$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is consistent when $S$ does not prove $\bot$.
nodes.title: Consistent set of formulas

nodes.summary: The depth $d(\varphi)$ of a first-order formula $\varphi$ is the nesting height of its implications and universal quantifiers: $\bot$, equations and relation atoms have depth $0$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ has depth $\max(d(\varphi), d(\psi)) + 1$, and $\forall \varphi$ has depth $d(\varphi) + 1$.
nodes.title: Depth of a formula

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the formulas $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ are a fixed enumeration, chosen by choice, of all first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and one bound variable: every such formula is $\varphi_k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Enumeration of formulas with one bound variable

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $L_F$ be the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$, with inclusion $\iota : L_F \to L$. Every bounded formula $\varphi$ of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and $n$ bound variables, each of whose symbols occurs in some formula of $F$, is the image under $\iota$ of a bounded formula of…
nodes.title: Bounded formulas lift to the finite-symbol sublanguage

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many symbols and let $S$ be a consistent set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ such that every free variable of every formula in $S$ is even. Then $S$ is contained in a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ with the Henkin property: for every formula $\varphi$ with one bound variable, if every instance $\varphi(t)$, for $t$ a term over $\mathbb{N}$, lies in…
nodes.title: Henkin extension of a consistent set

nodes.summary: Every consistent set $S$ of first-order formulas is contained in a maximal consistent set.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for first-order logic

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, with no countability hypothesis on its symbols. Every finite consistent set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is satisfiable: there are a nonempty $L$-structure $M$, in the universe of the function symbols of $L$, and an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which every formula of $F$ holds.
nodes.title: Finite satisfiability

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, with no countability hypothesis on its symbols. Every consistent set $S$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is satisfiable: there are a nonempty $L$-structure $M$, in the larger of the universes of the function symbols and the relation symbols of $L$, and an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which every formula of $S$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many symbols. Every consistent set $S$ of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is satisfiable: there are a nonempty $L$-structure $M$, in the universe of the function symbols of $L$, and an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which every formula of $S$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for first-order logic

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $L_F$ be the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$, with inclusion $\iota : L_F \to L$. Every term $t$ of $L$ whose variables are drawn from $\mathbb{N}$ and from $n$ bound variables, each of whose symbols occurs in some formula of $F$, is the image under $\iota$ of a term of $L_F$ with…
nodes.title: Terms lift to the finite-symbol sublanguage

nodes.summary: For bounded formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables, every symbol occurring in $\varphi$ occurs in $\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Symbols of the antecedent occur in an implication

nodes.summary: For bounded formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables, every symbol occurring in $\psi$ occurs in $\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Symbols of the consequent occur in an implication

nodes.summary: The finite set of function and relation symbols occurring in a bounded formula of a first-order language $L$, defined by recursion on the formula: $\bot$ has no symbols; an equation $t_1 = t_2$ has the function symbols of $t_1$ and $t_2$; an atomic formula $R(t_1, \dots, t_l)$ has $R$ together with the function symbols of $t_1, \dots, t_l$; an implication $\varphi \to \psi$ has the symbols of $\varphi$ and of…
nodes.title: Finite set of symbols of a formula

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term and $\varphi$ a first-order formula with $m + 1$ bound variables, and let $\varphi(t)$ be the instance obtained by substituting $t$ for the outermost bound variable. Every free variable of $\varphi(t)$ is a free variable of $\varphi$ or a variable of $t$.
nodes.title: Free variables of an instance

nodes.summary: Let $h : L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and let $\varphi$ be a bounded formula of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. The formula of $L'$ obtained from $\varphi$ by replacing each symbol by its image under $h$ has the same free variables as $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms preserve free variables

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be an $n$-ary function symbol, let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be terms over $\mathbb{N}$ and let $i < n$. For a term $u$, write $x[i := u]$ for $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $u$. If the equation $a = b$ lies in $\Delta$, then the equation $f(x[i := a]) = f(x[i := b])$ lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Congruence for function symbols in a maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th Henkin axiom is the Henkin axiom $\neg \forall \varphi_k \to \neg \varphi_k(c_k)$, where $\varphi_k$ is the $k$-th formula in the enumeration of formulas with one bound variable and $c_k$ is the $k$-th Henkin witness.
nodes.title: The $k$-th Henkin axiom

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open and let $c$ be a variable; write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. The Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is the formula $\neg \forall x\, \varphi \to \neg \varphi(c)$.
nodes.title: Henkin axiom

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the Henkin extension of a set $S$ of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is $S$ together with all Henkin axioms, the $k$-th Henkin axiom for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Henkin extension

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in a language with countably many symbols, and let $H_k$ be the $k$-th Henkin axiom. The stages $S_k$ are defined by $S_0 = S$ and $S_{k+1} = S_k \cup \{H_k\}$, so $S_k$ is $S$ together with $H_0, \dots, H_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Stages of the Henkin extension

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be such formulas. If $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ proves $\psi$, then $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Deduction theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $S$ be a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and let $c \in \alpha$ be a variable that occurs free neither in $\varphi$ nor in any formula of $S$. Then $S$ together with the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is consistent.
nodes.title: Adding a Henkin axiom preserves consistency

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $t$ write $\varphi(t)$ for the result of substituting $t$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains $\forall x\, \varphi$, then $\Delta$ contains $\varphi(t)$ for every term $t$.
nodes.title: Universal instantiation in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $u$ write $\varphi(u)$ for the result of substituting $u$ for $x$. If $s$ and $t$ are terms such that $\Delta$ contains the equation $s = t$ and the formula $\varphi(s)$, then $\Delta$ contains…
nodes.title: Substitution of equals in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: A term whose variables are free variables from $\mathbb{N}$ together with bound variables from the empty index set is lowered to the term over $\mathbb{N}$ of the same shape, in which every free variable $x$ stays $x$.
nodes.title: Lowering a term with no bound variables

nodes.summary: Let $h : L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and write $h(\varphi)$ for the formula of $L'$ obtained from a formula $\varphi$ of $L$ by replacing each symbol by its image under $h$. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then…
nodes.title: Derivations survive language homomorphisms

nodes.summary: A set $\Delta$ of formulas is maximal consistent when it is consistent and every consistent set of formulas containing $\Delta$ is contained in $\Delta$, that is, equals $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $R$ an $l$-ary relation symbol of $L$, and $t_1, \dots, t_l$ $L$-terms with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Then $R$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in the atomic bounded formula $R(t_1, \dots, t_l)$.
nodes.title: The relation symbol of an atomic formula occurs in it

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas of a language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. If $\Delta \cup \{\varphi\}$ is consistent, then $\varphi \in \Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets absorb consistent extensions

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. Every formula $\varphi$ that $\Delta$ proves lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets of first-order formulas are deductively closed

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $F$ a finite set of $L$-formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. The map from the symbols of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ to the symbols of $L$ sends every symbol of that sublanguage to a symbol occurring in some formula of $F$.
nodes.title: Symbols of a generated sublanguage occur in the generating formulas

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $F$ a finite set of $L$-formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and $\psi \in F$. Every symbol occurring in $\psi$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in some formula of $F$.
nodes.title: A symbol of a member of a set of formulas is a symbol of the set

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $f$ an $l$-ary function symbol of $L$, and $t_1, \dots, t_l$ $L$-terms with variables in $\alpha$. Then $f$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in the term $f(t_1, \dots, t_l)$.
nodes.title: The head function symbol of a term occurs in it

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, if $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$ and $S$ proves $\varphi$, then $S$ proves $\psi$.
nodes.title: Modus ponens for provability from sets

nodes.summary:
Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For every formula $\varphi$, $
eg\varphi \in \Delta$ if and only if $\varphi 
otin \Delta$; so exactly one of $\varphi$ and $
eg\varphi$ lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets decide every formula

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. If $S$ proves $\bot$, then $S$ proves every formula $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Ex falso for provability from sets

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages. For an $L$-term or bounded $L$-formula $x$, write $h(x)$ for the term or bounded formula of $L'$ obtained by replacing every symbol by its image under $h$. Let $t$ be an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables. Then $h$ applied to the instantiation of…
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms commute with instantiation in formulas

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages. For an $L$-term or $L$-formula $x$, write $h(x)$ for the term or formula of $L'$ obtained by replacing every symbol by its image under $h$. If $s$ and $t$ are $L$-terms with free variables in $\alpha$, then $h$ applied to the formula $s = t$ is the formula $h(s) = h(t)$.
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms preserve equations

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and for an $L$-term $u$ write $h(u)$ for the $L'$-term obtained by replacing every function symbol by its image under $h$. Let $t$ be an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $s$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables. Then $h$ applied to the instantiation of $t$ for the outermost bound variable (the one with…
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms commute with instantiation in terms

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and for an $L$-term $u$ write $h(u)$ for the $L'$-term obtained by replacing every function symbol by its image under $h$. Let $t$ be an $L$-term with variables in $\alpha$ and $g \colon \alpha \to \beta$ a map. Then $h$ applied to the term obtained from $t$ by renaming each variable $a$ to $g(a)$ equals the term obtained from $h(t)$ by the same…
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms commute with renaming variables

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and for an $L$-term $u$ write $h(u)$ for the $L'$-term obtained by replacing every function symbol by its image under $h$. Let $s$ be an $L$-term with variables in $\beta$ and $g$ a map assigning to each $b \in \beta$ an $L$-term $g(b)$ with variables in $\gamma$. Then $h$ applied to the term obtained from $s$ by substituting $g(b)$ for each…
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms commute with substitution in terms

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, with no countability hypothesis, $T$ a theory of $L$ (a set of sentences), and $\varphi$ an $L$-formula with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. Then $\varphi$ is provable from the sentences of $T$, each regarded as a formula with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, if and only if $\varphi$ holds in every nonempty model of $T$ under every assignment of elements of the model to the…
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness for arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many function and relation symbols, whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$. For every theory $T$ of $L$ and every formula $\varphi$ of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, $\varphi$ is provable from the sentences of $T$, viewed as formulas over $\mathbb{N}$, if and only if $\varphi$ holds under every assignment of the variables in…
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of first-order natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\neg\varphi\}$ is not consistent.
nodes.title: Provability as inconsistency with the negation

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\neg\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ is not consistent.
nodes.title: Refutability as inconsistency

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$, with no restriction on the number of symbols. Let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$, all with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. If for every $L$-structure $M$ with carrier in universe $\max(u, v)$ and every assignment $e : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which all formulas of $S$…
nodes.title: Strong completeness for arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many function and relation symbols, whose function symbols live in universe $u$. Let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$, all with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. If for every $L$-structure $M$ with carrier in universe $u$ and every assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which all formulas of $S$ hold, $\varphi$ also holds under $v$, then $\varphi$ is…
nodes.title: Strong completeness of first-order natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$, with no restriction on the number of symbols. Let $T$ be a theory of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. If $\varphi$ holds under every assignment of the variables in every nonempty model of $T$ whose carrier lies in universe $\max(u, v)$, then $\varphi$ is provable…
nodes.title: Completeness for arbitrary languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many function and relation symbols, whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$. Let $T$ be a theory of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. If $\varphi$ holds under every assignment of the variables in every nonempty model of $T$ whose carrier lies in universe $\max(u, v)$, then $\varphi$ is provable from…
nodes.title: Completeness of first-order natural deduction for theories

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every formula $\varphi$ with one bound variable, if $\Delta$ contains $\varphi(t)$ for every term $t$ (where $\varphi(t)$ is the result of substituting $t$ for the bound variable), then $\Delta$ contains $\forall x\,\varphi$. Then a formula $\psi$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ holds in the term model of…
nodes.title: Truth lemma for the first-order term model

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be an $n$-ary relation symbol, let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, $a$ and $b$ be terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $i < n$. If $\Delta$ contains $a = b$ and contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $a$, then $\Delta$ contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $b$.
nodes.title: Replacing an argument of a relation symbol by an equal term

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, then the set obtained from $S$ by renaming every free variable $x$ to $2x$ in each of its formulas is consistent.
nodes.title: Doubling the variables preserves consistency

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables with $\beta$ infinite, and let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ be any map. If $\varphi$ is derivable from the list of hypotheses $\Gamma$ in natural deduction, then the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by renaming each free variable $x$ to $f(x)$ is derivable from the list obtained by renaming the free variables of each formula of $\Gamma$ in the same way.
nodes.title: Renaming free variables along an arbitrary map preserves derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables, let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ further variables reserved for binding by enclosing quantifiers. If two maps $f, g : \alpha \to \beta$ agree on every variable from $\alpha$ that occurs free in $\varphi$, then renaming the variables of $\varphi$ from $\alpha$ along $f$ and along $g$ gives the same formula.
nodes.title: Renaming depends only on the free variables

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For every finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the inclusion into $L$ of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ is injective on function symbols and on relation symbols.
nodes.title: The inclusion of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas is injective

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For a finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, this is the language homomorphism from the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ into $L$ that sends each function symbol and each relation symbol to itself.
nodes.title: Inclusion of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For a finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, this is the set of those formulas $\psi_0$ of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$, with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, whose image under the inclusion of that sublanguage into $L$ belongs to $F$.
nodes.title: Preimage of a finite set of formulas in its sublanguage

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For every finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the map sending each symbol of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ to the same symbol of $L$ is injective.
nodes.title: The symbol map of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas is injective

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For a finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, this map sends each function symbol (respectively relation symbol) of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ to the same function symbol (respectively relation symbol) of $L$, with the same arity.
nodes.title: Symbols of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas as symbols of the language

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ has as its $n$-ary function symbols the $n$-ary function symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$, and as its $n$-ary relation symbols the $n$-ary relation symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$.
nodes.title: Sublanguage of a finite set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $s$ be a term of $L$ with variables in a type $\beta$, and let $g$ and $g'$ assign to each variable in $\beta$ a term of $L$ with variables in a type $\gamma$. If $g(a) = g'(a)$ for every $a \in \beta$, then substituting $g$ into $s$ gives the same term as substituting $g'$ into $s$.
nodes.title: Term substitution depends only on the values of the substitution

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For a finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, this map sends each symbol of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ to the same symbol of $L$, regarded as an element of the finite set of symbols occurring in $F$.
nodes.title: Symbols of the sublanguage as symbols occurring in a finite set of formulas

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of first-order formulas of a language $L$ with free variables indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, the symbols of $F$ are the finite set of function and relation symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$, that is, the union over $\psi \in F$ of the finite sets of symbols occurring in $\psi$.
nodes.title: Symbols of a finite set of formulas

nodes.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the canonical assignment sends each variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ to $[x]$, the class of the variable term $x$ in the term model of $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Canonical assignment of the term model

nodes.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the term model of $\Delta$ is the set of terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ modulo the equivalence relation that identifies $s$ and $t$ when the formula $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Term model of a maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. Provable equality in $\Delta$ is the equivalence relation on $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ under which $s \sim t$ holds exactly when the equation $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Provable equality of terms

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. The term structure of $\Delta$ is the $L$-structure whose domain is the set of $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in which an $n$-ary function symbol $f$ sends terms $t_1, \dots, t_n$ to the term $f(t_1, \dots, t_n)$, and an $n$-ary relation symbol $R$ holds of $t_1, \dots, t_n$ exactly when the atomic…
nodes.title: Term structure of a set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and let $t_1$, $t_2$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Every symbol occurring in $t_1$ occurs in the atomic formula $t_1 = t_2$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_1$ is contained in that of $t_1 = t_2$.
nodes.title: Symbols of the left side of an equation

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and let $t_1$, $t_2$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Every symbol occurring in $t_2$ occurs in the atomic formula $t_1 = t_2$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_2$ is contained in that of $t_1 = t_2$.
nodes.title: Symbols of the right side of an equation

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an $l$-ary function symbol of a first-order language $L$ and let $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$ be terms of $L$ in variables from $\alpha$. For every $i < l$, every symbol occurring in $t_i$ occurs in the term $f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$: the finite set of symbols of $t_i$ is contained in that of $f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$.
nodes.title: Symbols of an argument of a function application

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an $l$-ary relation symbol of a first-order language $L$ and let $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. For every $i < l$, every symbol occurring in $t_i$ occurs in the atomic formula $R(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_i$ is contained in that of $R(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$.
nodes.title: Symbols of an argument of a relational atomic formula

nodes.summary: The finite set of symbols occurring in a term $t$ of a first-order language $L$, a finite subset of the function and relation symbols of $L$, is defined by recursion on $t$: it is empty when $t$ is a variable, and when $t = f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$ for an $l$-ary function symbol $f$ it consists of $f$ together with the symbols occurring in each of $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$.
nodes.title: Finite set of symbols of a term

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation on a type $\beta$, let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a property of $n$-tuples $x = (x_i)_{i < n}$ in $\beta$. Suppose that for every tuple $x$, every position $i$ and all $a, b \in \beta$ with $r(a, b)$, if $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $a$, then $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $b$. nodes.title: Replacing arguments one at a time

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a first-order formula whose variables are natural numbers together with $n$ variables reserved for quantifiers. Its variable bound $b(\varphi)$ is one more than the largest natural number occurring as a free variable of $\varphi$, or $1$ when there is none; it is a strict upper bound on these free variables.
nodes.title: Variable bound of a formula

nodes.summary: Let $\phi : L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages and let $t$ be a term of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. The finite set of free variables from $\alpha$ occurring in the image $\phi(t)$ of $t$ under $\phi$ equals the finite set of those occurring in $t$.
nodes.title: Language homomorphisms preserve the free variables of a term

Logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
